the results of the present study are promising and suggest the potential of using capillary plasma stored in dried blood spots as a substitute for venous plasma in future epidemiologic and clinical studies.

there are significant differences in the concentrations of protein biomarkers between capillary plasma and venous plasma, which should be taken into consideration when interpreting results of studies using capillary plasma.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of filter paper is a viable alternative to venous plasma in the assessment of protein biomarkers, but the use of filter-paper samples should be carefully considered in relation to the study objectives.
